headline: Vendor booths
lead: Food trucks, cooking booths, drinks, snacks, crafts, merchant booths, activity booths, nonprofit info tables for Elk Grove Lunar New Year Tết 2027.

meta.description: Apply for a vendor booth on Eventeny for Elk Grove Lunar New Year Tết 2027. See fees, spots left, and how selection works.

waitlist.title: Apply for single booth or an entire zone
waitlist.bodyAfter: Round 1 closed Nov 5. Round 1 decisions were around Nov 10. Official vendor questions and invitations use **contact@eglny.com** and Eventeny only — don’t treat other Gmail addresses as from the organizing team.
waitlist.partnerIntro: Two ways to join the map: apply for a standard booth on Eventeny, or inquire about a named Custom Zones corner.

paths.title: Single booth on Eventeny
paths.body: Food, drinks, snacks, crafts, merchant, activity, and nonprofit info booths — apply through Eventeny.

paths.title: Custom Zones
paths.body: A named corner on the festival map — decorate it yourself or ask us to help bring your block to life.

cta.label: Apply on Eventeny
cta.note: Sign in or create a free Eventeny account. Most applicants pay a **$25** application deposit when they apply for a single booth. Nonprofit, community info, and free kids activity tables pay no deposit — and the free kids activity form does not ask for a credit card. Questions: **contact@eglny.com**.

notes: **Onsite cooking** means you cook or prep and **sell food to guests** for the whole weekend — not a staged live-demo booth.

**Vegetarian-focused cooking:** One of the **15** onsite cooking spots is reserved for a booth whose **core menu is vegetarian** — not a meat cook that also offers one vegetarian dish. Apply for onsite cooking on Eventeny and describe your menu; we offer that reserved seat when a vegetarian-focused cook fits.

**Same food type:** We limit how many booths sell the same kind of **cooked food** or **drink** so the festival has variety. **Onsite cooking** and **Drinks and snacks only:** strong limit — we avoid duplicate hot-food categories and drink types. If more than one vendor wants a limited type, we rank applications and offer in that order. **Snacks only** sits in the open merchant-style pool — we do **not** hard-cap snack vendors by type.

Weekend fee stacks **booth fee** + **refundable** cleanup deposits + County TFF when needed + a **COI** if your booth type requires one. COI dollar lines are short-term policy **estimates** (~$70 food · ~$50 exhibitor/power) — buy anywhere that meets the limits under Fees. Skip TFF if your MEV or MFF already covers the weekend. Cooking and drinks lock with a **partial booth payment**; the rest is due later. Also budget the **$25** application deposit at apply (credited toward the booth fee if selected).

**Paid guest activities** (face painting, balloon art, timed challenges, etc. where guests pay) → **Merchant / craft / paid activity** at **$150** on the Merchants & corporate app — not Corporate / marketing (**$500**), and not a free kids activity table.

fees.title: Fees and terms
fees.intro: Fees are for the **whole weekend** (Saturday and Sunday). We expect vendors to **staff both days** — there are no single-day booths. Same prices as on Eventeny. There is no early-bird discount — applying early helps you get a decision sooner in Round 1.

sections.title: Application deposit
body: Food, merchant, craft, and corporate booths pay **$25** when you apply.
bullets: If we accept you → the $25 counts toward your booth fee
If we don’t select you → we refund the $25

If we select you but you don’t pay by the deadline → you lose the $25, and we offer that booth **right away** to the next person on the selection waitlist for that booth type — not to Round 2 new applicants
If that happens in Round 1 → you move to the Round 2 waitlist without paying another deposit

sections.title: Nonprofit and kids tables
bullets: Nonprofit / community info: **no** application deposit; **$75** only if approved
Free kids activity (guests don’t pay): use the **Free kids activity tables** app — no fee, no card
Paid kids / guest activity → use **Merchant / craft / paid activity** ($150)

sections.title: Booth pad and footprint
body: Disclose your setup size on the application so we can place you correctly.
bullets: **Merchant, craft, snacks, and activity pads:** about **10×10**.
**Canopy cooking:** about **10×30** (includes roughly **5 feet** into grass / meridian for your generator).
**Food trucks and trailers:** dedicated pads; we can accommodate large units (up to about **10×40**). Tell us your length and pull-in needs when you apply.
Canopy cooking uses the same onsite-cooking lane and fee as a truck or trailer — layout assigns the pad type after you’re selected.

sections.title: Table and chairs
body: Paid vendor booths get **one standard table and two chairs**. Festival volunteers set them up before the weekend and take them down after.
bullets: **Tent / canopy is optional** and not included with the booth fee — an open pad with no canopy is fine. If you want shade: bring your own (straight-leg, fits fully in your pad, weighted; no staking into asphalt; permanently affixed fire-resistant / CPAI-84 fabric label) **or** add the optional **Basic $150** weekend canopy rental on Eventeny (labeled 10×10 popup + pad weights; we reserve with our festival partner and drop at load-in). Not the FTF sponsor Premium Tent ($900) or Gold Premium sponsor booth.
**Free kids activity tables:** the festival provides furniture for kids programming (it may not be one table and two chairs).
Need more furniture? Bring your own.

sections.title: Power and generators
body: Booth pads do **not** have shared electrical outlets. If you need power (freezer, electric griddle, lights, POS, etc.), bring your own quiet generator and/or battery pack.
bullets: Disclose generator use on your application. Generators must be fenced or guarded and meet Fire spacing rules.
Propane equipment (griddles, fryers, etc.) is allowed when it meets Fire / LPG rules (tanks, clearances, extinguisher).
Using electrical power or a generator also means you need a COI by the Jan 29 deadline (see Insurance below).

sections.title: Locking your booth
body: An offer only holds until the pay-by date. **Paying the booth fee locks your spot** — cleanup deposits do not.
bullets: **Round 1 — cooking** (canopy, food truck, or trailer): pay **$375 of the $750** booth fee by **Fri, Nov 20, 2026** to lock. The rest of the booth fee (**$350** after your $25 deposit credit) plus cleanup deposits are due **Fri, Jan 29, 2027**, or you give up the booth.

**Round 1 — Drinks and snacks only:** pay **$250 of the $500** booth fee by **Fri, Nov 20, 2026** to lock. The rest of the booth fee (**$225** after your $25 deposit credit) plus cleanup deposits are due **Fri, Jan 29, 2027**, or you give up the booth.
**Round 1 — everyone else** (Snacks only, merchant, corporate, nonprofit): pay the **full booth fee** by **Fri, Nov 20, 2026** to lock. Cleanup deposits are due **Fri, Jan 29, 2027**.
**Round 2:** pay the booth fee (and any deposits due) by **Fri, Jan 29, 2027** — or when you’re approved, if that’s later.

sections.title: Trash and cooking deposits
body: Food, merchant, and corporate booths also pay refundable cleanup deposits. They’re charged on **Fri, Jan 29, 2027** (or when you’re approved, if later). These deposits do **not** lock your booth.
bullets: **$100 trash** — every food, merchant, and corporate booth. You get it back when the pad is left clean — no trash, packaging, or abandoned goods.

**$500 cooking cleanup** — only if you cook on site (trucks/trailers, open flame, grills, fryers — including enclosed trailers with electric equipment). You get it back when there’s no pad damage from cooking.
Pre-packaged / no-cook food → trash deposit only
after: **Trash deposit examples that can hold or reduce a refund:** leftover boxes of merch or product, bags of trash, cardboard, packaging, a vinyl ground tarp left behind, or other items left on or beside your pad.
**Cooking cleanup examples that can hold or reduce a refund:** grease or oil stains, spilled fryer oil, burn marks, scorched pavement, or similar pad damage from cooking equipment.

sections.title: Deposit refunds
body: Cleanup deposits are refunded after the festival when your assigned pad(s) pass inspection. We aim to finish clean refunds **within about 30 days** after the event. If the park is still assessing a hold, it can take longer — we’ll email you.
bullets: **Morning of the festival:** as staff walk the vendor pads, each vendor reviews, signs, and returns a **booth-pad condition sign-off** and notes any concerns about their pad(s).
**After the event:** we do a **joint walkthrough with Cosumnes CSD / park staff**. We photograph issues, mark pad locations, and match them to the morning sign-offs.

**If there’s an incident on your pad:** we email you that the related deposit is **on hold** while we coordinate repair or cleanup cost with the park. Only the affected deposit is held; clean unrelated deposits still follow the normal refund path.
**Damage liability cap:** you are **not** billed for full park repair costs beyond the deposit. The related deposit is the **maximum** we withhold for that incident.
**First-time incidents:** you get a **warning**, and we document the incident in your vendor record. We track compliance over time; **repeat incidents** can affect future applications.

**Before you leave:** we recommend a short phone **video of your empty pad** that states your **business name, date, and time**. Keep it in case of a dispute (for example, if another vendor dumps trash on your pad after you leave).

sections.title: Temporary Food Facility (TFF) permit
body: If you sell food, drinks, snacks, or sealed take-home food, Sacramento County needs a Temporary Food Facility permit for the weekend. That fee is **separate** from the booth fee — we collect the County’s fee and pass it through at cost.
bullets: Already have a valid multi-event (MEV) or mobile food facility (MFF) permit that covers this event → send us your permit number; no TFF fee
Need a single-event TFF → we file with the County and charge their fee: **$116** for pre-packaged / low risk, or **$258** for food prep / high risk (County FY 2026–27 rates)
Charged after you’re approved, usually with the Jan 29 deposits

sections.title: Cancellations and refunds
body: Cancel by **Fri, Jan 15, 2027** (Round 2 application close) → we refund booth fees you’ve paid **in full**. Cancel after that date through **Fri, Jan 29, 2027** → we refund booth fees you’ve paid, minus a **cancel fee of 25% of the booth fee (minimum $50)**. After Jan 29, **no booth-fee refund** — the festival is already planned around your booth.
Elk Grove Park is our planned venue; permits are still in progress. If the festival can’t happen there, we refund deposits and booth fees in full (no cancel fee).
Weather: for each festival day that gets canceled, you get a **2028 credit** for half the booth fee — not cash. Only a venue cancellation is refunded in cash.

sections.title: Insurance (COI)
body: You do **not** need a certificate of insurance (COI) when you apply. Food booths, and any booth using electrical power or a generator, must upload a current general liability COI by **Fri, Jan 29, 2027** (same day as full booth payment and cleanup deposits) — or when you’re approved, if that’s later. Your booth isn’t fully confirmed until we review an acceptable COI.
bullets: **Who needs a COI:** every food booth on the Food app — including drinks, snacks, and sealed / prepackaged take-home food — plus any merchant, nonprofit, or kids booth that uses electrical power or a generator
**Who does not:** basic non-food booths with no power can confirm coverage in the vendor agreement (no COI upload)
**Coverage:** commercial general liability, occurrence form · **$1,000,000** each occurrence · **$2,000,000** general aggregate · must cover **Sat–Sun, Feb 13–14, 2027**

**Additional insured (list all three):** Cosumnes Community Services District, its officials, employees, agents, and authorized volunteers · Vietnamese American Community of Sacramento (VACOS) · Community Partners Advocate of Little Saigon Sacramento (cPALSs), as co-host
**Certificate holder:** Elk Grove Lunar New Year Tết 2027 / VACOS · 9950 Elk Grove-Florin Road, Elk Grove, CA 95624
after: You can upload a COI with your application if you already have one. Otherwise wait until closer to Jan 29. We’ll email accepted food and power vendors these guidelines again before the due date.

Need to buy a short-term policy? Rough estimates for a 2-day booth are about **$70** (food) and **$50** (exhibitor / power) — or use any insurer that meets the limits above. Free kids activity tables: COI, when required, may be **potentially sponsored**.

sections.title: Hours and load-in
body: Booth fees cover **both festival days** — we don’t offer single-day booths. Public hours are **11 AM–7 PM** Sat–Sun, Feb 13–14, 2027. Primary load-in is **Friday, Feb 12** (exact window in your vendor onboarding packet); same-day gates open around **7 AM** both mornings. Tear-down is after **7 PM Sunday**.

Vehicles are **drop-off only**. Be out of booth zones by **~10 AM** both days unless you’re granted an exemption. Exempt vehicles (food trucks / trailers placed for the weekend, or other written exemptions) stay put and **cannot move during public hours**. Plan for Fire inspection about **9–10 AM Saturday** with your pad ready and clear of non-exempt vehicles. Leaving early or bringing gear later means carting from the vendor reserved parking lots.

You may leave equipment secured on your assigned pad overnight Sat→Sun. Overnight site security is planned; still lock valuables and cover gear. The festival is not liable for theft or damage to vendor property.
after: Exact load-in, vehicle cutoffs, and tear-down times come in your vendor onboarding packet and may be updated for park or Fire needs.

timeline.title: How selection works
timeline.intro: We review applications in **two rounds**. Early applicants can lock a booth sooner. We also save some spots for strong later applications. The steps are the same in both rounds.

rounds.label: Round 1 — Closed
rounds.note: Most spots (~70–80%). Decisions around Nov 10. **Pay the booth fee by Nov 20 to lock your seat:** onsite cooking pays **$375 of $750**; Drinks and snacks only pays **$250 of $500**; everyone else pays the full booth fee. Miss Nov 20 → that seat goes **right away** to the next Round 1 waitlisted vendor for that booth type; you lose the $25 deposit and move to the Round 2 waitlist (no new deposit). Cooking and drinks vendors who locked still owe the rest of the booth fee plus cleanup deposits by Jan 29, or they give up the booth.

rounds.label: Round 2 — Open now
rounds.note: The seats we held back (~20–30%). Unpaid Round 1 seats are **not** thrown into this open pool — they go first to the Round 1 selection waitlist. Decisions around Jan 22 cover held-back seats and people still waiting (including unpaid Round 1 selectees). Pay by Jan 29. **Food and snack applicants:** wait until we publish the Round 1 food vendors and their menus before you apply. That list shows what’s already taken, so you can see if your type might waitlist — or whether you should apply with something different.

timeline.pathIntro: Everyone waits for a decision batch. Then one of these happens:

steps.title: Apply
steps.body: Submit on Eventeny with the $25 application deposit (required to be considered — nonprofit, community info, and kids activity tables pay no deposit). You don’t need insurance when you apply. Food booths and power/generator booths upload a COI later, by Fri, Jan 29, 2027, with full payment and deposits.

steps.title: Wait for selection
steps.body: We review everyone in that round together — not first-come, first-served. Food booths are ranked for how well the menu fits the festival. Other booths are reviewed for overall fit.

steps.title: One of three outcomes
steps.body: You’ll get one of these results.

outcomes.title: Offer sent
outcomes.body: You’re selected. Accept the offer (food vendors may get a recommended festival menu), then **pay by the deadline to lock your booth** (Round 1 onsite cooking: $375 of $750 by Nov 20; Drinks and snacks only: $250 of $500 by Nov 20; everyone else: full booth fee by Nov 20).
outcomes.next: Once that payment clears, you’re on the map. Round 1 cooking and drinks vendors still owe the rest of the booth fee plus cleanup deposits by Jan 29.

outcomes.title: Selection waitlist
outcomes.body: You’re next in line for that booth type. If a selected vendor misses the pay-by, we offer **that same seat to you right away** — we don’t hold it for Round 2 new applicants. **If you weren’t first pick for a limited food type,** you can stay on this waitlist for a possible promotion, **or** submit a new Round 2 application for a different food type that isn’t already taken. Separately: if **you** were selected in Round 1 and didn’t pay by Nov 20, you move to the Round 2 waitlist (no new deposit) and wait for Round 2 decisions around Jan 22. We may promote waitlisted applicants through **Sat, Feb 6, 2027**; after that we stop assigning new seats from the waitlist.
outcomes.next: A waitlist spot is not a reserved booth until you get an offer and pay. If you’re still unassigned after Feb 6, we start refunding the $25 application deposit on **Sun, Feb 7, 2027**.

outcomes.title: Declined
outcomes.body: Not selected for this festival season. If you paid the $25 application deposit, we refund it (waitlist refunds begin **Sun, Feb 7, 2027** for applicants still unassigned after the Feb 6 promote cutoff).

steps.title: Pay → official vendor
steps.body: Your offer only lasts until the pay-by date. Pay on time and you’re on the map. **Miss Round 1’s Nov 20 booth-fee lock** and that seat goes to the next Round 1 waitlisted vendor right away; you lose the $25 deposit and join the **Round 2 waitlist** (no new deposit). **Round 1 cooking and drinks vendors** who locked with the half booth fee but miss the **Jan 29** remainder + deposits **give up the booth** (same: next on the selection waitlist). Cancel by Jan 15 for a full booth-fee refund; after Jan 15 through Jan 29 for a refund minus the cancel fee; after Jan 29, no booth-fee refund.

timeline.footnote: Dates can shift a little if we need to. Spot counts by booth type were set with Round 1 decisions (around Nov 10).

criteria.title: Selection criteria
criteria.intro: We look at the whole round of applications together — not whoever paid first. Food applicants are ranked within their type. Craft, merchant, and info booths are reviewed for overall festival fit.
criteria.factorsIntro: For onsite cooking and Drinks and snacks only applicants, here’s roughly how much each factor counted in Round 1 and how much it counts in Round 2 (each column adds up to about 100%):

rows: Strong menu / festival fit — see [Food menu](/food/) for examples
Clear specialty (focused menu, not everything under the sun)
Dietary and guest needs — see [Food menu](/food/) for examples
Guest / family fit for this festival
Can this booth succeed with our expected crowd size?
Worked with our festivals before (Elk Grove LNY / Great Lantern)
Compliance readiness (permits, insurance, fire and pad rules)
Local Elk Grove ties and cultural anchors
Active food social media (real posts — not just a handle or follower count)
Earlier application deposit (when other scores are close)

criteria.factorsNote: A dash (—) means that factor did not apply in that round. Percents are approximate.

restrictions.title: Restrictions
deny: Adult-oriented businesses or products — including tobacco, drugs, pornography, firearms, and dating services
Organizations that practice or promote discrimination in employment or services
restrictions.salesIntro: Even approved vendors may not display or sell:
sales: Firecrackers, fireworks, firearms, weapons, or other dangerous items
Vulgar, offensive, sexually explicit, or obscene materials
restrictions.footnote: We may ask you to remove any product or service that doesn’t fit a family festival. That call is final.
